newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia police seize heroin, marijuana in raids.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia police seize heroin, marijuana in raids.

text.p: Police have seized 162 kg (356 pounds) of illegal drugs and arrested 13 suspected drug traffickers during raids in and around the Malaysian capital of Kuala Lumpur, newspapers reported on Wednesday.

Narcotics police chief Salleh Mat Som said police over 13 days had raided a condominium used as a heroin processing centre, a hotel room and several houses. They found 21 kg of heroin, 141 kg of marijuana and heroin processing equipment.
Police also seized 325 kg of caffeine, which is not illegal but is used in a cocktail mix with heroin before the narcotic is sold on the streets, a police narcotics official said.
Salleh was quoted in The Star as saying the drugs were believed to have been smuggled from southern Thailand into Malaysia's northeast state of Kelantan.

He told The New Straits Times: "We believe drug trafficking syndicates in the Klang Valley (around the capital) and city which rely on their supply from southern Thailand will now find themselves in a fix."
Police gave no total street value for the drugs, but said the heroin alone could be processed and sold for 31 million ringgit ($12.5 million).
